title: Planning Loops That Terminate
objective: After this lesson you will be able to implement ReAct-style plan-act-observe loops with iteration caps and progress detection, distinguish stuck (escalate) from slow (continue), and log loop trails for post-hoc analysis.
why: 'Think step by step, use tools as needed' loops forever on hard tasks: repeated identical tool calls, planning without acting, acting without observing. Termination by construction (caps + progress criteria + stuck escalation) plus trail logging converts hopeful loops into bounded, debuggable workhorses — the engine room of every agent harness.

blocks.text: The **ReAct loop**: reason (plan next step from state) → act (tool call) → observe (result into state) → repeat until done or budget exhausted. Each iteration is one bounded unit: max iterations cap total work, per-iteration timeouts bound stalls, and the done-condition (answer ready? task complete?) exits early. Unbounded 'while not done' loops are hangs awaiting hard inputs.

blocks.caption: Plan/act/observe with caps and trails — termination structural

blocks.text: Caps bound worst cases; **progress detection** exits stuck loops early: no new information in K iterations (repeated tool calls, identical observations) → escalate with the trail, don't burn remaining budget. Stuck signatures: same action thrice, observations unchanged, plan oscillating between two steps. Slow-but-progressing (new info each round) runs to completion — distinguish by information delta, never elapsed time alone.

blocks.caption: Repeat-counting on observations: stuckness detected, not hoped away

blocks.title: Bound the loop
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok=true iters=3 with the fetch/fetch/answer trail — then the stuck twin exhausting budget with reason. Termination both ways: done-flags finish work, budgets finish loops.

items: ReAct bounded: caps + per-iteration timeouts + done-conditions + trail logs
Stuck (no information delta) escalates early; slow (new info) runs on — distinguish by delta
Trails make loops debuggable post-hoc: every iteration recorded with kind + note

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice loops and map both outcomes. (b) Add progress detection (repeat-counting on notes) that escalates the stuck twin at 2 repeats instead of budget 3 — state what changes in the trail. (c) Write the done-condition for a research task (sufficient sources?) with the sufficiency rule stated.
hints: Baseline: ok=true/3 iters with fetch/fetch/answer trail; stuck twin budget-exhausted at 3.
Progress watch on result.note: second identical note trips stuck-escalation (faster than budget, with reason).
Done-condition: ≥3 independent sources covering all sub-questions (sufficiency = coverage, not count alone).
exercise.why: Budget termination (caps), progress termination (delta detection), and done-conditions (sufficiency rules) are the three loop exits — each verified, with trails proving which fired.
exercise.code: // Triple-exit pattern: done-flags, progress-trip, budget-cap — logged which.

quiz.q: Loop repeats identical tool calls 12 times. Missing?
options: Progress detection + stuck escalation: no-information-delta trips early exit with trail, not budget burn
quiz.explain: Repeat patterns signal stuckness, not slowness. Delta detection escalates with evidence; caps merely bound damage.

quiz.q: Slow-but-progressing task hits iteration cap. Response?
options: Distinguish stuck (no delta → escalate) from slow (new info → extend or checkpoint-resume with justification)
quiz.explain: Caps bound worst cases; progress justifies extension. Information delta decides — extend with evidence, escalate without.

options: Step-by-step evidence: plan choices, observations, and which exit fired — debugging without inference
quiz.explain: Trails record decisions and outcomes per iteration: stuck patterns visible, attribution precise, fixes targeted.

summary: Bounded ReAct with trails, progress-trip escalation, sufficiency done-conditions. Loops terminate by construction — done, stuck, or budgeted, always logged.
